audit_items.proof_trace: Cache key omits the actual kzg_commitments being verified, including only the proof branches and block header hash. Two data columns with different commitments but identical proofs/headers share the same cache entry, allowing the second to bypass Merkle proof verification entirely.
audit_items.attack_scenario: Attacker sends valid DataColumn₁ with commitments_A to populate cache, then sends DataColumn₂ with malicious commitments_B but reusing the same proof and header. Cache hit at L368-369 skips verification at L375, accepting unverified commitments.
